name: eapol_sm_notify_config
prose: Passes a new network configuration to the EAPOL supplicant state machine (eapol_supp_sm.c:1554-1586; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns without effect if sm is NULL (1558-1559). It stores the config pointer in sm->config; with CONFIG_EAP_PROXY it also sets sm->use_eap_proxy from eap_proxy_notify_config (1561-1564). It returns if conf is NULL (1566-1567). It copies accept_802_1x_keys, required_keys, fast_reauth, workaround and wps into sm->conf (1569-1573). With CONFIG_EAP_PROXY and use_eap_proxy set it returns here (1574-1578). Otherwise (including builds without proxy support) and when the EAP state machine exists, it passes fast reauthentication, the workaround, the disabled flag and external SIM setting to the EAP layer (1580-1585).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the prose says the EAP layer is updated only when proxy support is compiled in and not in use, but the code also updates when proxy support is not compiled in - right (the #ifdef at 1574-1579 compiles the early return out). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: SM_STEP(SUPP_PAE)
prose: Generated step function of the IEEE 802.1X supplicant PAE state machine (macro invocation SM_STEP(SUPP_PAE) at eapol_supp_sm.c:365-449); it returns nothing and may change sm->SUPP_PAE_state through SM_ENTER_GLOBAL and SM_ENTER. The global transitions are tested first, in this order: LOGOFF when a user logoff is pending and not yet sent and the port is enabled and not initializing; DISCONNECTED when the port control is Auto and the port mode differs, or initialize is set, or the port is not enabled; S_FORCE_AUTH and S_FORCE_UNAUTH when the port control asks for a forced mode that is not yet set (367-381). If none of them applies, it switches on the current state: LOGOFF goes to DISCONNECTED when the user logoff is cleared; DISCONNECTED goes to CONNECTING; CONNECTING goes to CONNECTING again, AUTHENTICATED, AUTHENTICATING, RESTART or HELD depending on startWhen, startCount, portValid, eapSuccess, eapFail and eapolEap; AUTHENTICATING may first set portValid and call eapol_done_cb when the key requirements allow it, then goes to AUTHENTICATED, HELD or CONNECTING; HELD goes to CONNECTING or RESTART; AUTHENTICATED goes to RESTART or DISCONNECTED; RESTART goes to AUTHENTICATING when eapRestart is clear; the unknown and forced states do nothing (382-448). So the state can change even when no global guard fires.
note: [R:right] reviewer: says the state is unchanged if no global guard fires, but the switch can transition (for example DISCONNECTED to CONNECTING) - right (389-391). Name in the packet was "SUPP_PAE_step"; the file defines the step through the macro SM_STEP(SUPP_PAE). Read in full.

name: SM_STEP(SUPP_BE)
prose: Generated step function of the IEEE 802.1X supplicant backend state machine (macro invocation SM_STEP(SUPP_BE) at eapol_supp_sm.c:592-661); it returns nothing and may change sm->SUPP_BE_state. If initialize or suppAbort is set it enters INITIALIZE through SM_ENTER_GLOBAL (594-595). Otherwise it switches on the state: REQUEST logs a warning if both eapResp and eapNoResp are set and goes to RESPONSE (eapResp), RECEIVE (eapNoResp), FAIL (eapFail) or SUCCESS (eapSuccess), in that order of precedence (599-626); RESPONSE goes to RECEIVE; SUCCESS, FAIL and TIMEOUT go to IDLE; IDLE goes to FAIL, REQUEST or SUCCESS when suppStart is set together with eapFail, eapolEap or eapSuccess respectively; INITIALIZE goes to IDLE; RECEIVE goes to REQUEST, FAIL, TIMEOUT (authWhile is 0) or SUCCESS (627-659). The function does not use the EAP proxy or eap_key_available fields.
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: when use_eap_proxy is true but no proxy key is available, the code returns and never checks eap_key_available - not applicable to this function: SM_STEP(SUPP_BE) does not mention use_eap_proxy or eap_key_available at all (592-661); the remark concerns different code. Name in the packet was "SUPP_BE_step". Read in full.

name: p2p_build_wps_ie
prose: Appends a WPS vendor-specific information element for P2P to buf (p2p_build.c:742-841; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It needs at least 6 bytes of tailroom, writes the element id, a length placeholder and the WFA OUI, and adds the WPS version attribute, returning -1 on any failure (748-755). When all_attr is nonzero it adds the WPS State attribute with the value "not configured" (757-763). When pw_id is not negative it adds the Device Password ID attribute (765-774). When all_attr is nonzero it also adds the Response Type, UUID-E, manufacturer, model name, model number, serial number, primary device type, device name and configuration methods attributes (776-809). It adds the WFA vendor extension (811-812) and, when all_attr is nonzero and secondary device types exist, the secondary device type list (814-824). Then it adds the configured WPS vendor extensions, skipping any that does not fit (827-836), fills in the element length and returns 0 (840). Each of the tailroom checks and attribute builders returns -1 when it fails.
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: the prose claims the WPS State attribute is appended when all_attr is nonzero, but the code never builds it - wrong: p2p_build.c:757-763 writes ATTR_WPS_STATE with WPS_STATE_NOT_CONFIGURED when all_attr is set. Slice cut the head; function read in full except the debug lines and the final length fix-up (837-840).

name: p2p_process_go_neg_resp
prose: Processes a received P2P Group Owner Negotiation Response (p2p_go_neg.c:1214-1484; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns without effect if the peer device is unknown, has no WPS method, is not the current negotiation peer, the message does not parse, no response was awaited or the dialog token differs (1225-1249); otherwise it clears the wait flag and records the peer's 6 GHz capability. A missing status attribute goes to fail with INVALID_PARAMS. A nonzero status (a failure by the peer) clears go_neg_req_sent and, for "information currently unavailable", marks the peer not yet ready and waits up to 120 s, or else reports the failure with p2p_go_neg_failed; then it calls send_action_done and returns without building a confirmation (1251-1278). For a success status it requires the intended address, a GO intent of at most 15 (shifted) and a compatible GO role determination, a group id when it is the client, and a configuration timeout, going to fail with INVALID_PARAMS or INCOMPATIBLE_PARAMS otherwise (1296-1341). A missing Capability or P2P Device Info attribute is fatal only when CONFIG_P2P_STRICT is defined; otherwise it only logs (1280-1294). It then stores peer information, checks the device password id against the WPS method (INCOMPATIBLE_PROV_METHOD on mismatch), selects the operating channel when it is the GO (failure goes to fail), checks preferred channels, sets the state GO_NEG and records the intended address (1378-1447). At fail it builds a GO Negotiation Confirmation with the status, sends it, sets the pending action state and go_state only for a success status, and calls p2p_go_neg_failed for a nonsuccess status (1449-1483).
note: [R:right] reviewer: a non-success status returns before building the confirm; a missing capability/device info is fatal only under CONFIG_P2P_STRICT - right (1256-1277 return before 1449-1454; 1280-1294 have the #ifdef CONFIG_P2P_STRICT). Partly read: 1214-1345 line by line and the tail 1420-1484; the middle (1345-1420: wfd and operating-channel attributes and the password-id switch) was scanned only by gotos.

name: p2p_check_pref_chan
prose: Applies the driver's preferred frequency list when a P2P group is being formed (p2p_go_neg.c:694-799; the packet name is right, the slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It does nothing if the driver does not provide a preferred frequency list, if preferred channels are configured, if a frequency is forced for the peer, or if an operating channel is set in the configuration (709-711). It fetches the list into p2p->pref_freq_list and returns if the call fails or the list is empty (714-721). It then removes from that list, by shifting later entries down, every frequency that is not acceptable: one with no channel mapping, one not in the local channels (and for a client not in the client channels), or a 6 GHz frequency when 6 GHz is not allowed with this peer (723-749). It logs the remaining list and looks for the peer's operating frequency in it among the entries allowed for the role (p2p_pref_freq_allowed); if found it sets the operating class and channel and copies the configured channel set, then returns (768-783). Otherwise it calls p2p_check_pref_chan_no_recv when the message has no preferred frequency list and p2p_check_pref_chan_recv when it does (793-798).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: it does not remove unacceptable frequencies, it only checks p2p_pref_freq_allowed when matching dev->oper_freq - wrong: the loop at p2p_go_neg.c:726-749 removes unacceptable entries from the list with os_memmove; p2p_pref_freq_allowed is the extra test at 771. The function starts at 694 (slice cut the head); read in full; the two _recv helpers not read.

name: p2p_process_prov_disc_resp
prose: Processes a received P2P Provision Discovery Response (p2p_pd.c:1306-1603; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns without effect if the frame does not parse, or, when P2PS provisioning is active, if the P2PS validation fails (the message is freed in the second case) (1320-1326). It reads the status, the group address, the advertisement MAC and id and the connection capability (swapping group owner and client roles) (1329-1354). It returns if the peer is unknown or has no pending request, and if the dialog token differs (1360-1378). It clears the pending PD state, and when the received WPS configuration methods differ from the requested ones it reports a rejected provisioning through prov_disc_fail, frees the message and goes to out (1380-1410). The rest (1413-1560) records the accepted configuration methods in the peer flags, handles the P2PS status and password ids, may report failure through prov_disc_fail, and records the interface address. At out it clears the peer's req_config_methods and calls send_action_done; if the peer is flagged PD_BEFORE_GO_NEG it clears that flag and continues with p2p_connect_send and returns (1564-1572). Otherwise it calls prov_disc_resp for a successful non-P2PS response or the P2PS cases and, if the state is P2P_PD_DURING_FIND, stops listening and continues the find (1589-1602).
note: [R:n/a] fixed-unreviewed in the packet; checked against the source. Partly read: head (1306-1420) and tail (1560-1603); the middle (1420-1560) was scanned only by its goto lines (1528, 1554) and not read, so the description of that part is general.

name: p2p_prov_disc_req
prose: Starts a P2P Provision Discovery exchange with a peer (p2p_pd.c:1687-1752; slice cut the head); it returns 0, -1 or the result of p2p_send_prov_disc_req. It looks up the peer; an unknown peer, or one known only from a probe request, frees p2ps_prov and returns -1 (1694-1702). With no config methods and no P2PS provisioning it returns -1 (1707-1710). A deferred P2PS status copies the previous method (1712-1716). It then clears the peer's wps_prov_info, replaces the stored P2PS provisioning with the new one (the previous one is freed), stores the requested methods and sets or clears the join flag (1719-1727). If the P2P state is not idle, search or listen-only it logs that the request is postponed and returns 0 (1729-1735). Otherwise it records user_initiated_pd and the forced frequency, sets the retry count for a user-initiated request, advances the peer's dialog token (skipping 0) and returns p2p_send_prov_disc_req(p2p, dev, join, force_freq) (1737-1751). This function does not set pending_action_state itself.
note: [R:right] reviewer: claims pending_action_state remains P2P_PENDING_PD on any send failure; early p2p_send_prov_disc_req failures occur before it is set - right: in p2p_send_prov_disc_req (p2p_pd.c:1610-1683) the returns at 1621, 1630, 1662 and 1667 come before pending_action_state is set at 1671; only the failure at 1677 follows it. Function read in full; p2p_send_prov_disc_req read only by its pending_action_state and return lines.

name: radius_client_retransmit
prose: Retransmits a RADIUS message from the client list (radius_client.c:374-545; slice cut the head); it returns 0 to keep the entry, 1 to have the caller remove it, or -1 on a TLS encryption failure. It selects the accounting or authentication side, its TLS connection and server count; if that socket is not open it initialises it and, with several servers, fails over, returning 0 when the failover removed messages (391-427). It counts a request or a timeout and retransmission for the server (408-413, 429-434). An interim accounting message is dropped: it calls the interim error callback and returns 1 (437-446). A negative socket returns 1 (448-452). If the TLS connection is not yet ready it jumps to not_ready without sending and without incrementing the attempt counters, but still reaches the code that sets next_try and doubles next_wait (455-459, 536-542). For an accounting message it updates the Acct-Delay-Time and gets a new identifier (463-489). If the accumulated attempts reached the failover limit it returns 1 (492-496). Otherwise it increments attempts and accu_attempts, encrypts the message when TLS is used (failure returns -1), sends it, and on a send error that the handler treats as fatal frees the buffer and returns 0 without setting the next try time (499-531). Then it frees the buffer, sets next_try to now plus next_wait, doubles next_wait up to RADIUS_CLIENT_MAX_WAIT and returns 0 (534-544).
note: [R:mixed] reviewer: the TLS-not-ready path returns before incrementing attempts/next_try, so the retry schedule is not advanced - half right: attempts and accu_attempts are not incremented there (499-500 are after 459), but the not_ready label at 536 still sets next_try and next_wait (539-542), so the schedule is advanced. Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: radius_server_request
prose: Handles a received RADIUS Access-Request on the built-in server (radius_server.c:1357-1555; slice cut the head); it returns 0, -1 or -2. It finds the session from the State attribute (or uses a forced session); a request with a State but no matching session is rejected and returns -1, and without State a new session is created (failure rejects and returns -1) (1372-1402). A retransmission (same port, identifier and authenticator as the last request) counts a duplicate, resends the stored last reply and returns 0, or returns -1 if there is no stored reply (1404-1428). Without an EAP attribute it uses MAC ACL handling when configured (a NULL reply returns -1, otherwise it jumps to send_reply), and otherwise counts a dropped packet and returns -1 (1430-1443). With EAP data it passes it to the EAP server state machine and takes a reply from it; if the method is pending it stores the message and the sender and returns -2 (1454-1475); an unusable state counts a dropped packet and returns -1 (1476-1482). It marks the session complete when the state machine succeeded or failed, builds the reply with radius_server_encapsulate_eap (1485-1497), and in send_reply counts the reply type, sends it, and stores it with the port, identifier and authenticator as the last reply (1499-1538); with no reply it only counts a dropped packet and does not set last_reply (1539-1542). When the session is complete it replaces the removal timeout with one of RADIUS_SESSION_MAINTAIN seconds (1544-1551) and returns 0 (1554).
note: [R:mixed] reviewer: no session-removal timeout is scheduled; the dropped-reply path does not set last_reply - the first part is wrong: radius_server.c:1544-1551 cancels and registers radius_server_session_remove_timeout for a complete session; the second part is right: 1539-1542 does not set last_reply. Slice cut the head; function read in full except debug lines.

name: radius_server_eap_pending_cb
prose: Callback invoked when a pending EAP method of the built-in RADIUS server has a result (radius_server.c:2616-2652; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns if data is NULL (2622-2623). It searches all clients' sessions for the one whose eap equals ctx and which has a stored last_msg (2625-2634); if there is none it logs and returns (2636-2639). It takes the stored message out of the session (clearing last_msg), calls eap_sm_pending_cb(sess->eap) (only the EAP state machine is passed, not the message), and calls radius_server_request again with that message, the stored sender information and the session forced (2641-2648). If that returns -2 (the method is pending again) it returns and the message is kept by the request function; otherwise it frees the message (2648-2651).
note: [R:right] reviewer: msg is not handed to eap_sm_pending_cb(); only sess->eap is passed there - right (2643). Slice cut the head; function read in full; eap_sm_pending_cb not read.

name: wpa_tdls_process_tpk_m1
prose: Processes a received TDLS Setup Request (TPK Handshake Message 1) on the responder side (tdls.c:1942-2317; the packet name is correct but the slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It returns -1 if the frame is too short (1967-1968). It finds or adds the peer entry (a failure goes to error); for an existing peer with an established link it tears the old link down and clears the peer, and for an existing peer for which it already initiated a setup it returns -1 when its own address is lower than the sender's, otherwise it disables the link of the earlier attempt and continues (1978-2012). It then parses and checks the link identifier, RSN and other elements: many malformed or inconsistent elements go to error with a TDLS status code (goto error at 2036-2176), a missing key lifetime or a lifetime below 300 seconds gives UNACCEPTABLE_LIFETIME (2165-2177). With a valid RSN it builds the peer's RSN element, and stores the validated lifetime in peer->lifetime (2273) and derives the TPK with wpa_tdls_generate_tpk (2278); unless a testing flag skips it, it adds the peer to the driver (a failure goes to error) (2281-2289). It then sets tpk_in_progress and sends TPK Message 2; a send failure disables the link and goes to error (2294-2300). It returns 0 (2309). The error label sends a setup error response with the status and frees the peer entry, then returns -1 (2311-2316).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: the annotation says the peer entry is filled with lifetime/TPK, but the code only validates the lifetime and never stores it - wrong for the lifetime: tdls.c:2273 `peer->lifetime = lifetime;` and 2278 derives the TPK. Partly read: head (1960-2012), the lifetime part (2160-2180), 2262-2317; the many element checks in between (2013-2160 and 2180-2262) were scanned only by their goto lines.

name: wpa_tdls_process_tpk_m3
prose: Processes a received TDLS Setup Confirm (TPK Handshake Message 3) (tdls.c:2655-2813; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or the result of the link enabling, and -1 on failure. It finds the peer entry by address and returns -1 if there is none (2671-2679). It cancels the retry timeout for the setup response (2680). A too-short frame, a nonzero status, or a failure of any of the following element checks goes to error (2682-2790): the RSN, link identifier, fast transition and timeout (lifetime) elements are compared with those stored for the peer. It adds or sets the peer in the driver, and if the TPK handshake had not succeeded yet it enables the link; a negative result of wpa_tdls_enable_link goes to error, otherwise ret holds that result and is returned (2794-2809). The error label tears the link down with wpa_tdls_do_teardown (reason TDLS_TEARDOWN_UNSPECIFIED) and returns -1 (2810-2812).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: error paths only disable the peer link; wpa_tdls_do_teardown is not called, and the negative enable_link return is omitted - wrong: the error label calls wpa_tdls_do_teardown (tdls.c:2811) and a negative wpa_tdls_enable_link goes to error (2803-2806). Partly read: head (2659-2695) and tail (2790-2813); the element checks in between (2695-2790) were scanned only by their goto lines.

name: wpa_eapol_key_send
prose: Sends an EAPOL-Key frame from the supplicant (wpa.c:91-207; slice cut the head); it returns the result of wpa_sm_ether_send or -1. It takes ownership of msg and frees it at the out label on every path (204-206). If the destination and the stored BSSID are both zero it tries to read the BSSID and uses it as the destination (101-117). When a MIC is in use (mic_len nonzero) and a key_mic buffer is requested it needs a PTK with a KCK (otherwise -1) and computes the MIC, going to out with -1 if that fails (119-135). When no MIC is used (the AES-SIV case) it needs a PTK with a KEK, allocates a buffer, and encrypts the key data with aes_siv_encrypt, going to out with ret still -1 if the allocation or the encryption fails; on success it replaces msg by the encrypted frame (136-195); without CONFIG_FILS this branch goes to out with -1 (197). It then sends the frame with wpa_sm_ether_send, notifies the EAPOL state machine of the transmitted key frame, and frees msg (202-206).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits the -1 return when aes_siv_encrypt fails during AES-SIV encryption - right (183-187: free the temporary buffer and goto out with ret = -1). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: wpa_supplicant_process_3_of_4
prose: Processes EAPOL-Key message 3 of the 4-way handshake in the supplicant (wpa.c, wpa_supplicant_process_3_of_4 ending at 2807; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It validates the key information flags (encrypted key data, install and secure must be set), parses the key data elements, checks the GTK and IGTK elements against the key-data flags, the ANonce against the stored one and the key length against the pairwise cipher; any failure goes to the failed label, which deauthenticates with WLAN_REASON_UNSPECIFIED (2583-2770, 2805-2806). Some paths return silently (2687, 2696). When the checks pass it installs the PTK (if the install flag is set; a failure goes to failed), sets the state to WPA_GROUP_HANDSHAKE (2746), handles the GTK and IGTK (a failure goes to failed), sends message 4 (wpa_supplicant_send_4_of_4) and reports negotiation completion with wpa_supplicant_key_neg_complete, then sets rekey offload, adds a PMKSA entry for Suite B, handles a transition-disable element, sets msg_3_of_4_ok to 1 and returns (2776-2803). It does not set WPA_4WAY_HANDSHAKE on the success path.
note: [R:right] reviewer: the prose says it sets WPA_4WAY_HANDSHAKE, but the code only sets WPA_GROUP_HANDSHAKE on success - right (2746). Partly read: grep of the state, install, send and failed lines (2560-2830) and 2776-2807; the validation chain (2583-2770) and the GTK/IGTK handling were scanned only by their goto and return lines. The function's name was taken from the packet; the definition head was not displayed.

name: wpa_supplicant_get_pmk
prose: Finds or obtains the PMK for the current 4-way handshake (wpa.c:311-510; slice cut the head); it returns 0, -1 or -2. If a PMKID is given and no PMKSA is selected it looks the entry up in the cache; none found sets abort_cached (317-333). A PMKID that matches the selected entry installs the PMK from the cache and notifies the EAPOL layer (335-341 and the lines after it). Otherwise, for 802.1X key management, it asks the EAPOL state machine for the MSK: on success it derives and caches a PMKSA, and a new PMK that does not match the given PMKID returns -1 (a mismatch message), a match clears abort_cached (430-460). With FT key management over an FT protocol association and no PMK it logs that the handshake continues without a PMK or PMKID and changes nothing (461-464), so sm->pmk, pmk_len and cur_pmksa are not updated in that case. Otherwise a failure to get the key logs a warning, cancels a selected PMKSA (setting abort_cached) or returns -1 if none was selected and abort_cached is not set (465-479). When abort_cached remains set for plain 802.1X (not Suite B, FT or OSEN) it sends an EAPOL-Start to trigger full authentication and returns -2 (-1 if the frame cannot be allocated) (482-506). Otherwise it returns 0 (509).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the FT continue-without-PMK return 0 does not update sm->pmk/pmk_len or cur_pmksa as the prose claimed - right (461-464 contain only the log). Partly read: 311-345 and 430-510; the lines 345-430 (EAPOL MSK retrieval and PMKSA creation) were not read.

name: wpa_sm_set_assoc_rsnxe
prose: Stores the station's own RSNXE for the association (wpa.c:4991-5020; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It returns -1 if sm is NULL (4993-4994). It frees the old RSNXE, then clears the stored pointer and length when ie is NULL or len is 0, otherwise it stores a copy made with os_memdup and returns -1 if the copy fails, in which case sm->assoc_rsnxe has been set to NULL by that assignment and not left dangling (4996-5008). If SSID protection is enabled and the stored RSNXE does not advertise the SSID protection capability, it disables SSID protection (5011-5017). It returns 0 (5019).
note: [R:right] reviewer: on os_memdup failure sm->assoc_rsnxe is set to NULL, not left dangling - right (5004-5006; assoc_rsnxe_len is left at its old value on that failure). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: wpa_ft_process_response
prose: Processes an FT (fast BSS transition) response on the supplicant (wpa_ft.c:584-777; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. All failure paths go to fail, which frees the parsed information elements (wpa_ft_parse_ies_free) and returns ret; the same free also runs on success (774-776). For an over-the-DS action it drops the response unless an over-the-DS transition is in progress for the same target AP (603-616). It fails if FT is not enabled for the key management, if the elements cannot be parsed, or if the mobility domain element, FT element, ANonce, SNonce (which must equal the stored one), R0KH-ID, R1KH-ID, the PMKID in the RSN element or the PMF requirement do not match (618-686). It stores the R1KH-ID and ANonce, derives PMK-R1 and then the PTK (with a KDK if configured) (688-716) and the LTF key seed when needed (722-727). It generates the reassociation request elements with wpa_ft_gen_req_ies and passes them to wpa_sm_update_ft_ies (743-747), marks the peer authenticated, installs the PTK (a failure sets set_ptk_after_assoc), sets ft_completed and, for the action frame case, copies the target AP address into sm->bssid, and returns 0 (749-773).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: claims the parsed IEs are freed on failure, but the code has no such free - wrong: wpa_ft.c:775 calls wpa_ft_parse_ies_free(&parse) at the fail label, which is reached both by every goto fail and by the success path. Partly read: head (584-740) and tail (737-777) line by line; the debug lines were skipped.

name: mp_exptmod_fast
prose: Computes Y = G^X mod P with a fixed-window method and a Montgomery, diminished-radix or 2^k reduction (libtommath.c:2952-3235; the packet name was truncated, the function is the static mp_exptmod_fast); it returns MP_OKAY on success or an error code. The window size is chosen from the bit length of X (capped at 5), and the table entries M[1] and M[1<<(winsize-1)] to M[(1<<winsize)-1] are initialised; a failed mp_init clears the entries made so far and returns the error (2965-3003). The reduction is chosen from redmode: 0 uses Montgomery reduction (a failed setup, or an unsupported build configuration, leaves err as the setup result or MP_VAL), 1 uses diminished-radix reduction, and any other value uses 2^k reduction, so redmode is not restricted to 0 and 1 in the code (3006-3053). It initialises res (failure goes to LBL_M, 3056-3058), builds the table and runs the exponentiation loop (3067-3211 not read in detail), does a final Montgomery reduction when redmode is 0 (3213-3223), and only on success exchanges res into Y (mp_exch) and sets err to MP_OKAY (3226-3227). Any failing step jumps to LBL_RES or LBL_M, which free res and the initialised table entries; Y is changed only by that final exchange, and the function returns err (3228-3234).

name: tlsv1_server_process_handshake
prose: Dispatches one received TLS record to the handler of the server's current handshake state (tlsv1_server_read.c:1269-1320; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. An alert record with fewer than 2 bytes sends a fatal decode-error alert and returns -1; any other alert sets the state to FAILED and returns -1 (1272-1283). Otherwise it switches on conn->state and calls tls_process_client_hello, tls_process_certificate, tls_process_client_key_exchange, tls_process_certificate_verify, tls_process_change_cipher_spec or tls_process_client_finished, returning -1 if the handler returns nonzero; an unexpected state logs and returns -1 (1285-1314). After a successful handler, if the record is a handshake record, it adds the buffer (buf, *len) to the handshake hash with tls_verify_hash_add (1316-1317), including when the state was CLIENT_FINISHED; the length value used is whatever the handler left in *len. It returns 0 (1319).

name: x509_certificate_chain_validate
prose: Validates a certificate chain against a list of trusted certificates (x509v3.c:2138-2259; slice cut the head); it returns 0 if the chain is valid (or CA trust is disabled with no trusted list) and -1 otherwise, setting *reason in the failing cases. It walks the chain from the first certificate. For each certificate it first sets issuer_trusted to 0, but after the chain has been found trusted at some certificate the walk only clears issuer_trusted for the remaining certificates and does nothing else (2153-2159). A failing step returns -1 at once, leaving issuer_trusted of later certificates untouched. Unless time checks are disabled it requires the current time to lie in the validity period (2161-2171). When there is a next certificate it requires that its subject equals this one's issuer, that it is a valid issuer, that a path length constraint is not exceeded and that its signature on this certificate verifies (2173-2214). It looks up the issuer in the trusted list; if found it requires the trusted certificate to be a valid issuer and its signature on this certificate to verify, then sets this certificate's issuer_trusted to 1 and marks the chain trusted (2216-2242). If no certificate was found trusted it returns -1 when a trusted list is given, and otherwise only logs that CA validation was disabled (2245-2254); it returns 0 (2258).

Slice cut the head; function read in full (the *reason assignments are in lines filtered out as debug output).

name: ieee80211_radiotap_iterator_next
prose: Advances a radiotap header iterator to the next present field (radiotap.c:234-396; slice cut the head); it returns 0 with this_arg, this_arg_index and this_arg_size set when a field is found, -ENOENT at the end of the fields, or -EINVAL for an inconsistent header. It loops over bitmap bits (237-395). It returns -ENOENT when the extension bit is not set at an index that is a multiple of 32 (243-245) or when an unknown bit is found in the radiotap namespace itself (267-270). A set bit selects alignment and size: namespace and extension bits take no data, the vendor namespace bit takes 6 bytes with alignment 2, and other bits use the current namespace table (or an override); a field of unknown size in a vendor namespace ends that namespace's data by skipping to _next_ns_data (251-284). It aligns _arg (298-302). For a vendor namespace bit it returns -EINVAL if the 6-byte vendor header lies beyond max_length, reads the OUI and sub-namespace, looks up the namespace, reads the vendor data length vnslen, sets _next_ns_data = _arg + size + vnslen, and adds vnslen to size only when the namespace is not registered (304-323); so vnslen is not checked against max_length for a registered namespace, and only the later check of _arg against max_length applies (343-346). It records the current field, advances _arg and returns -EINVAL if that passes max_length (329-346). Then it handles the namespace and extension bits (switching namespace, reading the next bitmap word) without returning a field, except that an unregistered vendor namespace is returned as a raw field (349-383); any other bit is a hit and returns 0 (384-394).

Slice cut the head; function read in full.

prose: Timer callback that ends a WPS push-button (PBC) session (wps_registrar.c:1021-1028; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. name: wps_build_cred
prose: Builds the Credential attribute for the WPS registrar's M8 message into msg (wps_registrar.c:1618-1834; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. When the registrar has skip_cred_build set it jumps straight to skip_cred_build, so wps->cred is not filled in and no Credential attribute is added; it then only appends the registrar's extra credential, if there is one, and returns 0 (1625-1626, 1827-1833). A credential supplied in wps->use_cred is copied and used; a multi-AP backhaul station with a configured backhaul SSID gets that SSID and key; otherwise the credential is built from the AP's SSID, the enrollee's masked authentication type (WPA2-PSK, then WPA-PSK, then open; none of these returns -1) and the encryption type, key and MAC address (1629-1678, the rest 1679-1784 not read). With use_provided it optionally adds a stub credential for testing, then allocates a 200-byte buffer (return -1 if that fails), builds the credential with wps_build_credential (failure frees the buffer and returns -1), appends the attribute (type, length, data) and frees the buffer; the extra credential is appended after that, and it returns 0 (1785-1833).

Partly read: head (1618-1678) and tail (1785-1834); the middle (the key generation for PSK networks, 1679-1784) was scanned only by its return -1 lines (1699, 1711, 1728, 1734, 1768, 1775).

name: wps_registrar_get_msg
prose: Returns the next WPS message of the registrar side to send (wps_registrar.c:2100-2195; slice cut the head); it returns the message buffer or NULL and sets *op_code only on some paths. With UPnP and no internal registrar it takes the oldest pending UPnP message from the list (clearing the external-registrar pending state if ext_reg is above 1), sets *op_code to ACK, NACK or MSG by its type, frees the list entry, and returns the message, setting ext_reg to 1 if it was 0 (2105-2138); with an external registrar and no pending message it returns NULL (2141-2145). Otherwise it builds the message for the current state: SEND_M2 builds M2D when no device password is available and M2 otherwise, SEND_M2D builds M2D, SEND_M4, SEND_M6 and SEND_M8 build those messages, RECV_DONE builds a WSC ACK (op code ACK) and SEND_WSC_NACK builds a NACK (op code NACK); a message of type MSG sets *op_code to WSC_MSG (2148-2179). Any other state logs and returns NULL without setting *op_code (2180-2184). Only when the op code is WSC_MSG and the message was built, it replaces wps->last_msg with a copy of the message; if a build returns NULL, last_msg is not touched (2187-2192). It returns the message (2194).

name: wps_process_wsc_ack
prose: Processes a received WSC_ACK message on the registrar (wps_registrar.c:3112-3176; slice cut the head); it returns a wps_process_res. It returns WPS_FAILURE if the message does not parse, has no message type, or the type is not WSC_ACK (3119-3131). With UPnP, an external registrar, state RECV_M2D_ACK and subscribers, it returns WPS_CONTINUE if UPnP messages are pending and otherwise WPS_PENDING, before any nonce is compared (3133-3141). It returns WPS_FAILURE if the registrar nonce or the enrollee nonce is missing or differs from the stored one (3144-3155). For the state RECV_M2D_ACK it again may return WPS_CONTINUE or WPS_PENDING when UPnP subscribers exist, and otherwise logs that the negotiation is terminated (3157-3172). The function returns WPS_FAILURE at the end for every case that did not return earlier (3175), so a valid ACK without UPnP processing also gives WPS_FAILURE.

name: wps_registrar_add_nfc_pw_token
prose: Adds an NFC password token to the WPS registrar (wps_registrar.c:3692-3744; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It returns -1 if dev_pw_len exceeds WPS_OOB_DEVICE_PASSWORD_LEN, and for the connection handover password id returns -1 when no public key hash was given or it was not provided out of band (3699-3707); both checks happen before any existing token is removed. It then frees existing tokens with the same pw_id (3709), allocates a token (return -1 if that fails, with the old same-id tokens already freed), fills in the public key hash, password id, the OOB flag and the device password as an uppercase hex string (3711-3726), adds it to the list, sets selected_registrar, clears pbc, adds the wildcard authorized MAC, notifies the registrar about the selected change and restarts the selected-registrar timeout (3728-3738), and returns 0 (3743).

name: event_retry
prose: Re-queues a failed UPnP event for the next subscriber address, or gives up (wps_upnp_event.c:117-142; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It cleans up the event's HTTP client state (event_clean) (124). When do_next_address is nonzero it increments e->retry (127-130). If e->retry is not below the length of the subscription's address list it logs "Giving up" using e->addr->domain_and_port, deletes the event, sets s->last_event_failed and, if events remain queued, schedules sending later, then returns (131-138); otherwise it adds the event back at the end of the queue and schedules sending later (140-141). In that giving-up message e->addr is dereferenced, but event_addr_failure sets e->addr = NULL (wps_upnp_event.c:197) before calling event_retry(e, 0) (209), so in that call, if the address list has become no longer than e->retry, the NULL pointer is dereferenced in the log argument (133).

name: event_send_start
prose: Starts sending the next queued UPnP event to a subscriber (wps_upnp_event.c:270-310; slice cut the head); it returns 0 when the HTTP request was started and -1 otherwise. It returns -1 without changes if the address list is empty, an event is already current, or the event queue is empty (280-283). Otherwise it makes the dequeued event the current event and walks the address list to the entry numbered e->retry: if the list has fewer than e->retry entries it returns -1 (leaving the event as current), but when e->retry equals the list length the loop ends without a break, itry is not below e->retry, and the code goes on with e->addr left pointing at the list head position and not at a real address (288-293). It builds the message; failure calls event_addr_failure and returns -1 (295-299). It starts the HTTP client; failure frees the message, calls event_addr_failure and returns -1 (301-307); otherwise it returns 0 (309).

name: advertisement_state_machine_handler
prose: Timer callback that sends the next SSDP advertisement message of the WPS UPnP device (wps_upnp_ssdp.c:257-327; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It asks next_advertisement for the next message and its "is last" flag and returns without rescheduling if there is none (282-284). It sends the message to the SSDP multicast address and port; if sendto fails it logs and sets the next timeout to 10 seconds (291-296). If the send worked and this was the last message of the sequence it resets the state; for a "byebye" (ADVERTISE_DOWN) sequence it switches to ADVERTISE_UP and keeps the short default delay, and for an up sequence it sets a random delay of UPNP_CACHE_SEC/4 plus up to UPNP_CACHE_SEC/4 seconds and increments advertise_count (297-318). Otherwise it increments the state (319-321). It frees the message and registers itself again with eloop_register_timeout(next_timeout_sec, next_timeout_msec, ...) (323-326); the variable next_timeout_msec, whose default is 100, is passed as the microseconds argument of that call, so the default delay is 100 microseconds rather than 100 milliseconds.

name: wpa_bss_update
prose: Updates an existing BSS entry from a new scan result (bss.c:671-800; slice cut the head); it returns the (possibly reallocated) BSS. If the entry was already updated in this scan round it returns it unchanged when the old entry is associated or looks more current, otherwise it accepts the newer one (676-710). It computes the changes, resets the scan miss count, copies the new fields and IE lengths via wpa_bss_copy_res and removes the entry from the list (712-720). Unless a P2P IE would be lost (the IEs are then kept), it copies the new IEs in place when they fit; when they do not fit it reallocates the entry, and on success it updates the references to it (last_scan_res, current_bss, the ML probe bss and a pending connect) and copies the IEs, while on allocation failure it keeps the old entry without the new IEs and carries on (738-781). If the IEs changed it sets the HESSID and the MLD address from the multi-link element (782-794). It re-adds the entry at the list tail, calls notify_bss_changes and returns the entry; there is no early return after a failed realloc, so the notification still happens (795-799).

name: wpas_ctrl_nfc_report_handover
prose: Handles the control-interface command that reports an NFC handover (ctrl_iface.c:1826-1940; the packet name wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_nfc_report_handover does not exist); it returns the result of the handler it calls or -1. It parses "<role> <type> <req-hex> <sel-hex> [freq=N]" in place: an optional " freq=" value is read into forced_freq, and a missing role, type, request or select field returns -1 (1837-1866). It converts each hex string to a buffer; an odd length, an allocation failure or invalid hex returns -1 after freeing what it allocated (1868-1905). Then, by role and type, it calls wpas_wps_nfc_report_handover (INIT, WPS), wpas_ap_wps_nfc_report_handover and, if that fails with a negative result, wpas_er_wps_nfc_report_handover (RESP, WPS), wpas_p2p_nfc_report_handover with the initiator flag (INIT, P2P) or the forced frequency (RESP, P2P); any other combination logs and gives -1 (1910-1931). It frees both buffers and returns the handler's result (1933-1939).

name: ctrl_iface_get_capability_key_mgmt
prose: Writes the list of supported key management names into buf for the GET_CAPABILITY command (ctrl_iface.c:4255-4473; slice cut the head); it returns the number of characters in the list, 0 or -1. If res is negative: with strict it returns 0, otherwise it copies the default list "WPA-PSK WPA-EAP IEEE8021X WPA-NONE NONE" with os_strlcpy and returns its length, or -1 if it does not fit (4268-4276). Otherwise it picks key_mgmt from capa->key_mgmt_iftype[iftype] for a recognised interface type (an unknown iftype_str returns -1) or from capa->key_mgmt (4278-4287). It then appends the text of "NONE IEEE8021X" and one token for each capability bit set (WPA-EAP, WPA-PSK, WPA-NONE, FT and SHA-256 variants, SAE, SUITE-B, OWE, DPP, FILS, OSEN and others) with os_snprintf (4289-4467). When a snprintf call reports truncation the function returns pos - buf at once, which counts only the tokens written completely so far; the buffer text after that point is whatever os_snprintf left (it NUL-terminates a truncated write by its definition, which I did not read) (4290-4291, 4297-4298 and the matching lines). prose: Marks a D-Bus property of an object as changed and schedules the signal flush (dbus_new_helpers.c:859-900; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. (894-899); that macro is 5000 (dbus_new_helpers.c:843) and is passed as the microseconds argument, so the delay is 5000 microseconds (5 ms), not 5 seconds. name: wpas_dpp_gas_req_handler
prose: GAS server callback that handles a DPP Configuration Request (dpp_supplicant.c:4191-4302; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. It returns NULL if there is no authentication, it has not succeeded (neither authentication nor reconfiguration), or the sender is not the peer (4200-4204). If a configurator is waiting for the ACK of the Authentication Confirm, it assumes it was received, notifies success and clears the flag, and in the test mode that stops at the confirm returns NULL (4206-4222). It logs the request, builds the response with dpp_conf_req_rx and stores resp_ctx in auth->gas_server_ctx (4225-4231). Only in builds with CONFIG_DPP2: if there is no response because a certificate is not ready, it stores resp_ctx in config_resp_ctx, sets *comeback_delay to 500 and returns NULL (4233-4239). If there is no response because the configurator is waiting for the application's configuration, it formats the peer information (name, bands, MUD URL), reports DPP_EVENT_CONF_NEEDED, restarts the initial-response timeout for 50 ms and returns NULL (4242-4292). Otherwise it stores the response in conf_resp; with no response it reports DPP_EVENT_CONF_FAILED, deinitialises the authentication and clears wpa_s->dpp_auth; it returns resp (4295-4301).

name: wpas_select_network_from_last_scan
prose: Selects and connects to a network from the last scan results (events.c:2642-2809; slice cut the head); it returns 0, 1, 2 or -1. It returns 0 when the P2P management interface is in use or a mesh group was joined (2661-2675). It picks a network (wpa_supplicant_pick_network); if one is selected and roaming is not needed it returns 0 (after the preauth step for a new scan) (2679-2686). Otherwise it deauthenticates when switching to a different network from an authenticating state, connects and returns -1 when wpa_supplicant_connect fails, and returns 1 on a successful connect (2688-2710). If none is selected it tries to pick a new network and associates (2714-2719); otherwise, for the function's own scan request, it may trigger a 6 GHz scan and return 1 when wpas_trigger_6ghz_scan returns a negative value, which cannot happen because that function returns only 0 or 1 (2720-2723). With the P2P scan helper it can return 2 or 0, and later branches return 1 after starting an ANQP fetch, 0 after scheduling a new scan quickly for P2P provisioning, WPS or OWE transition cases, or schedule a normal scan or scheduled scan and report NETWORK_NOT_FOUND (2735-2805). The default return is 0 (2808).

name: multi_ap_set_4addr_mode
prose: Applies the Multi-AP backhaul station checks and 4-address mode after association (events.c:3059-3088; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It does nothing if there is no current network or it is not a Multi-AP backhaul station configuration (3061-3063). If the AP did not include a valid Multi-AP element it deauthenticates with WLAN_REASON_DEAUTH_LEAVING (3065-3069, 3086-3087). If the AP does not advertise backhaul support it accepts a fronthaul-only BSS only while WPS is active for the network and returns, otherwise it deauthenticates (3071-3081). If the AP advertises backhaul support it calls wpa_supplicant_set_4addr_mode (3083).

name: wpas_ml_parse_assoc
prose: Parses the Basic Multi-Link element of an association response into per-link information (events.c:3778-4030; the packet name ml_basic_parser does not exist, and the slice cut the head); it returns the number of links stored in ml_info or 0. It returns 0 if no valid links are set or no Basic Multi-Link element is present, or if defragmentation fails (3796-3801). Any malformed or mismatching content ends at out, which frees the defragmented buffer and returns 0: a too short element, a control field lacking the expected presence bits, a common info length different from the expected one or too large for the element, and an AP MLD address different from wpa_s->ap_mld_addr (3805-3861, 4027-4029). It clears ml_info before parsing (3808). It then reads the link id of the association link and the per-link STA profile sub-elements, recording for each link its id, BSSID and status code; a sub-element too short goes to out (3864-4023). On success it frees the buffer and returns the count i (4025-4026). On a failure after some entries were filled, ml_info keeps the entries already written, and the buffer behind ml is freed on both paths.

name: wpa_supplicant_event_assoc
prose: Handles the driver's association event in the supplicant (events.c:4132-4460; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It has several early returns (4145, 4151, 4164, 4171, 4181, 4187, 4222, 4228, 4268) and sets the state to WPA_ASSOCIATED (4196). It records already_authorized from the association information (4274). Unless the FT handshake is complete or the port is already authorized, it clears portEnabled and portValid of the EAPOL state machine; it notifies EAP success in some key management cases (PSK, DPP, OWE, FT completed, already authorized or a driver-authorized port) and sets portEnabled (4284-4294). With no key management or WPA-NONE, or in IBSS mode, it sets WPA_COMPLETED (after setting the key and cancelling the auth timeout); otherwise, when FT is not completed, it requests a 10-second authentication timeout (4296-4316). If FT is completed it sets WPA_COMPLETED and the EAPOL success and valid-port indications (4319-4327). If the driver does the 4-way handshake for PSK, it sets WPA_COMPLETED only when the driver already authorised the port and otherwise waits for the port-authorized event; for 802.1X with a driver-side 4-way handshake it only notifies portValid (4328-4355). The rest of the function (4357-4460 and the remaining handling) applies test overrides and sets the association information, which was not read.
